---
title: Submit a transaction to Stellar RPC
description: Use a looping mechanism to submit a transaction to the RPC.
---

This guide builds `submitTx`, a helper that sends a signed transaction to Stellar RPC and waits for the result. Other guides reuse it.

## Send statuses

[`sendTransaction`](/docs/data/apis/rpc/api-reference/methods/sendTransaction) returns right away with one of four statuses. Only `ERROR` is a final rejection.

| Status | Meaning | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PENDING` | The network accepted the transaction. It waits for a ledger. | Poll `getTransaction` for the result. |
| `DUPLICATE` | The network already has this transaction in its queue, for example from an earlier send. | Do not treat it as an error. Poll `getTransaction` for the result. |
| `TRY_AGAIN_LATER` | The network did not accept the transaction this time. Usually another transaction from the same source account still waits for a ledger. If you send a transaction again after it is in a ledger, you also get `TRY_AGAIN_LATER` for about 10 ledgers. | Wait, then send the same signed transaction again. |
| `ERROR` | The network rejected the transaction. `errorResult` has the reason. | Fix the transaction. But first call `getTransaction`: if you send a transaction again after it is in a ledger, you get `ERROR` (`txBAD_SEQ`) once those 10 or so ledgers pass. |

For more about these statuses and the errors behind them, see [Debugging errors](/docs/learn/fundamentals/contract-development/errors-and-debugging/debugging-errors).

## Wait for the result

[`getTransaction`](/docs/data/apis/rpc/api-reference/methods/getTransaction) returns `NOT_FOUND` until the transaction is in a ledger. `NOT_FOUND` does not mean that the transaction failed. The transaction can go into a ledger at any time until its time bound (`maxTime`) passes.

Poll until `getTransaction` returns `SUCCESS` or `FAILED`. If it still returns `NOT_FOUND` after a ledger closes later than `maxTime`, the transaction can never go into a ledger. Only then is it safe to build and send a new transaction.

<Warning>

`server.pollTransaction()` stops after a fixed number of attempts (30 by default) and then returns the last `NOT_FOUND` response. Do not treat that response as a failure. If you send a new transaction at that point, the network can apply both transactions, and you pay twice.

</Warning>

## The `submitTx` helper

<CodeGroup>

```typescript JavaScript
import { FeeBumpTransaction, Transaction } from "@stellar/stellar-sdk";
import { Api, Server } from "@stellar/stellar-sdk/rpc";

const RPC_SERVER = "https://soroban-testnet.stellar.org/";
const server = new Server(RPC_SERVER);

const sleep = (ms: number) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));

// Sends a transaction, then waits until it is in a ledger or has expired.
async function submitTx(
  tx: Transaction | FeeBumpTransaction,
): Promise<Api.GetTransactionResponse> {
  // A transaction can go into a ledger only until its time bound (maxTime).
  const inner = tx instanceof FeeBumpTransaction ? tx.innerTransaction : tx;
  const maxTime = Number(inner.timeBounds?.maxTime ?? 0);
  if (maxTime === 0) {
    throw new Error("Call setTimeout() so that the transaction can expire");
  }

  // TRY_AGAIN_LATER: send the same signed transaction again after a pause.
  let reply = await server.sendTransaction(tx);
  while (
    reply.status === "TRY_AGAIN_LATER" &&
    Number(reply.latestLedgerCloseTime) <= maxTime
  ) {
    await sleep(2000);
    reply = await server.sendTransaction(tx);
  }

  // ERROR: a transaction that is already in a ledger also returns ERROR
  // (txBAD_SEQ) when you send it again, so look it up before you throw.
  if (reply.status === "ERROR") {
    const known = await server.getTransaction(reply.hash);
    if (known.status === Api.GetTransactionStatus.NOT_FOUND) {
      throw reply;
    }
  }

  // Poll until the transaction is in a ledger or has expired.
  // NOT_FOUND means "not in a ledger yet", not "failed".
  while (true) {
    const result = await server.getTransaction(reply.hash);
    switch (result.status) {
      case Api.GetTransactionStatus.SUCCESS:
        return result;
      case Api.GetTransactionStatus.FAILED:
        throw result;
      case Api.GetTransactionStatus.NOT_FOUND:
        // A ledger closed after maxTime, so the transaction can never go
        // into a ledger. Only now is it safe to build a new transaction.
        if (Number(result.latestLedgerCloseTime) > maxTime) {
          throw new Error(`Transaction ${reply.hash} expired`);
        }
        await sleep(1000);
    }
  }
}
```

```python Python
import time

from stellar_sdk import FeeBumpTransactionEnvelope, SorobanServer, TransactionEnvelope
from stellar_sdk.soroban_rpc import (
    GetTransactionResponse,
    GetTransactionStatus,
    SendTransactionStatus,
)

RPC_SERVER = "https://soroban-testnet.stellar.org/"
server = SorobanServer(RPC_SERVER)


# Sends a transaction, then waits until it is in a ledger or has expired.
def submit_tx(
    tx: TransactionEnvelope | FeeBumpTransactionEnvelope,
) -> GetTransactionResponse:
    # A transaction can go into a ledger only until its time bound (max_time).
    inner = (
        tx.transaction.inner_transaction_envelope.transaction
        if isinstance(tx, FeeBumpTransactionEnvelope)
        else tx.transaction
    )
    time_bounds = inner.preconditions.time_bounds if inner.preconditions else None
    max_time = time_bounds.max_time if time_bounds else 0
    if max_time == 0:
        raise ValueError("Set a timeout so that the transaction can expire")

    # TRY_AGAIN_LATER: send the same signed transaction again after a pause.
    reply = server.send_transaction(tx)
    while (
        reply.status == SendTransactionStatus.TRY_AGAIN_LATER
        and reply.latest_ledger_close_time <= max_time
    ):
        time.sleep(2)
        reply = server.send_transaction(tx)

    # ERROR: a transaction that is already in a ledger also returns ERROR
    # (txBAD_SEQ) when you send it again, so look it up before you raise.
    if reply.status == SendTransactionStatus.ERROR:
        known = server.get_transaction(reply.hash)
        if known.status == GetTransactionStatus.NOT_FOUND:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Transaction rejected: {reply.error_result_xdr}")

    # Poll until the transaction is in a ledger or has expired.
    # NOT_FOUND means "not in a ledger yet", not "failed".
    while True:
        result = server.get_transaction(reply.hash)
        if result.status == GetTransactionStatus.SUCCESS:
            return result
        if result.status == GetTransactionStatus.FAILED:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Transaction failed: {result.result_xdr}")
        # A ledger closed after max_time, so the transaction can never go
        # into a ledger. Only now is it safe to build a new transaction.
        if result.latest_ledger_close_time > max_time:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Transaction {reply.hash} expired")
        time.sleep(1)
```

```go Go
package main

import (
  "context"
  "errors"
  "fmt"
  "time"

  "github.com/stellar/go-stellar-sdk/txnbuild"

  client "github.com/stellar/go-stellar-sdk/clients/rpcclient"
  protocol "github.com/stellar/go-stellar-sdk/protocols/rpc"
)

const rpcServer = "https://soroban-testnet.stellar.org/"

var server = client.NewClient(rpcServer, nil)

// Sends a transaction, then waits until it is in a ledger or has expired.
func submitTx(
  ctx context.Context,
  tx *txnbuild.GenericTransaction,
) (protocol.GetTransactionResponse, error) {
  var none protocol.GetTransactionResponse

  // A transaction can go into a ledger only until its time bound (MaxTime).
  inner, ok := tx.Transaction()
  if feeBump, isFeeBump := tx.FeeBump(); isFeeBump {
    inner, ok = feeBump.InnerTransaction(), true
  }
  if !ok {
    return none, errors.New("empty transaction")
  }
  maxTime := inner.Timebounds().MaxTime
  if maxTime == 0 {
    return none, errors.New("set a timeout so that the transaction can expire")
  }

  envelope, err := tx.MarshalText()
  if err != nil {
    return none, err
  }
  request := protocol.SendTransactionRequest{Transaction: string(envelope)}

  // TRY_AGAIN_LATER: send the same signed transaction again after a pause.
  reply, err := server.SendTransaction(ctx, request)
  if err != nil {
    return none, err
  }
  for reply.Status == "TRY_AGAIN_LATER" && reply.LatestLedgerCloseTime <= maxTime {
    time.Sleep(2 * time.Second)
    if reply, err = server.SendTransaction(ctx, request); err != nil {
      return none, err
    }
  }

  // ERROR: a transaction that is already in a ledger also returns ERROR
  // (txBAD_SEQ) when you send it again, so look it up before you fail.
  if reply.Status == "ERROR" {
    known, err := server.GetTransaction(ctx, protocol.GetTransactionRequest{Hash: reply.Hash})
    if err != nil {
      return none, err
    }
    if known.Status == protocol.TransactionStatusNotFound {
      return none, fmt.Errorf("transaction rejected: %s", reply.ErrorResultXDR)
    }
  }

  // Poll until the transaction is in a ledger or has expired.
  // NOT_FOUND means "not in a ledger yet", not "failed".
  for {
    result, err := server.GetTransaction(ctx, protocol.GetTransactionRequest{Hash: reply.Hash})
    if err != nil {
      return none, err
    }
    switch result.Status {
    case protocol.TransactionStatusSuccess:
      return result, nil
    case protocol.TransactionStatusFailed:
      return result, fmt.Errorf("transaction failed: %s", result.ResultXDR)
    }
    // A ledger closed after MaxTime, so the transaction can never go
    // into a ledger. Only now is it safe to build a new transaction.
    if result.LatestLedgerCloseTime > maxTime {
      return result, fmt.Errorf("transaction %s expired", reply.Hash)
    }
    time.Sleep(time.Second)
  }
}
```

```java Java
// Dependencies (Maven coordinates):
//   network.lightsail:stellar-sdk:6.0.0

import org.stellar.sdk.SorobanServer;
import org.stellar.sdk.TimeBounds;
import org.stellar.sdk.Transaction;
import org.stellar.sdk.responses.sorobanrpc.GetTransactionResponse;
import org.stellar.sdk.responses.sorobanrpc.GetTransactionResponse.GetTransactionStatus;
import org.stellar.sdk.responses.sorobanrpc.SendTransactionResponse;
import org.stellar.sdk.responses.sorobanrpc.SendTransactionResponse.SendTransactionStatus;

public final class SubmitTx {
  private static final String RPC_SERVER = "https://soroban-testnet.stellar.org/";
  private static final SorobanServer server = new SorobanServer(RPC_SERVER);

  // Sends a transaction, then waits until it is in a ledger or has expired.
  public static GetTransactionResponse submitTx(Transaction tx) throws InterruptedException {
    // A transaction can go into a ledger only until its time bound (maxTime).
    TimeBounds timeBounds = tx.getTimeBounds();
    long maxTime = timeBounds == null ? 0 : timeBounds.getMaxTime().longValue();
    if (maxTime == 0) {
      throw new IllegalArgumentException("Call setTimeout() so that the transaction can expire");
    }

    // TRY_AGAIN_LATER: send the same signed transaction again after a pause.
    SendTransactionResponse reply = server.sendTransaction(tx);
    while (reply.getStatus() == SendTransactionStatus.TRY_AGAIN_LATER
        && reply.getLatestLedgerCloseTime() <= maxTime) {
      Thread.sleep(2000);
      reply = server.sendTransaction(tx);
    }

    // ERROR: a transaction that is already in a ledger also returns ERROR
    // (txBAD_SEQ) when you send it again, so look it up before you throw.
    if (reply.getStatus() == SendTransactionStatus.ERROR) {
      GetTransactionResponse known = server.getTransaction(reply.getHash());
      if (known.getStatus() == GetTransactionStatus.NOT_FOUND) {
        throw new IllegalStateException("Transaction rejected: " + reply.getErrorResultXdr());
      }
    }

    // Poll until the transaction is in a ledger or has expired.
    // NOT_FOUND means "not in a ledger yet", not "failed".
    while (true) {
      GetTransactionResponse result = server.getTransaction(reply.getHash());
      if (result.getStatus() == GetTransactionStatus.SUCCESS) {
        return result;
      }
      if (result.getStatus() == GetTransactionStatus.FAILED) {
        throw new IllegalStateException("Transaction failed: " + result.getResultXdr());
      }
      // A ledger closed after maxTime, so the transaction can never go
      // into a ledger. Only now is it safe to build a new transaction.
      if (result.getLatestLedgerCloseTime() > maxTime) {
        throw new IllegalStateException("Transaction " + reply.getHash() + " expired");
      }
      Thread.sleep(1000);
    }
  }
}
```

</CodeGroup>

RPC sends `latestLedgerCloseTime` as a string, so the JavaScript helper converts it with `Number()` before it compares it with `maxTime`. The Python, Go and Java SDKs already parse it into an integer.

In Go, pass a `*txnbuild.Transaction` as `txnbuild.NewGenericTransactionWithTransaction(tx)` and a fee-bump transaction as `txnbuild.NewGenericTransactionWithFeeBumpTransaction(tx)`.

In Java, `SorobanServer.sendTransaction` takes only a `Transaction`, so this helper does not accept a `FeeBumpTransaction`. The [fee-bump guide](/docs/build/guides/transactions/fee-bump-transactions) shows how to send one with a plain JSON-RPC request.

<Warning>

Remember: You should always handle errors gracefully! This is a fail-hard and fail-fast approach that should only be used in these examples.

</Warning>
